1	# Interactive CLI contract (add, init) - decided 2026-11-23, owner-approved direction
2	
3	When prompts run
4	- stdin AND stderr are terminals and output is text: prompts.
5	- --format json, or stdin or stderr not a terminal: never prompt. add without flags -> E214; init without --yes -> E240; each names the flags to pass.
6	- Blank or whitespace --summary: error before any prompt.
7	
8	Ending a run
9	- Completed: path written; next-step line on stderr; exit 0.
10	- Esc or Ctrl-C at any prompt: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 130.
11	- Declining the review / write confirmation: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
12	- Editor saves nothing or exits non-zero: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
13	- External kill -INT at a prompt: default signal behaviour (signal 2), nothing written; documented limit: terminal may need `reset`.
14	- SIGINT while $EDITOR runs (unix): ignored by Callisto (git launch_editor precedent); the editor decides. No signal thread anywhere.
15	
16	Editor and inputs
17	- $VISUAL else $EDITOR; blank = unset; none -> inline summary prompt.
18	- Unusable editor (split error, not found, non-UTF-8): one warning naming the variable and command, then the inline prompt, answers kept.
19	- Whitespace-only inline summary: re-prompt.
20	- Changed packages first and ticked, exactly as status reports; detection failure -> one warning, all unticked.
21	- JSON mode: exactly one report on stdout; notes once on stderr.
22	
23	init and origin
24	- Missing or non-hosted origin: one note; preview and init continue unbound; the remote value is never printed.
25	- --workflow / --artifact-target without a hosted origin: E299, help names git remote get-url --push origin / set-url --push.
26	
27	Exit codes: 0 success or decline; 1 error; 2 usage; 130 cancelled at a prompt.
28	
29	Proposed additions (2026-11-24, pending owner approval)
30	- TERM=dumb never prompts (E214/E240), as non-TTY.
31	- While init prompts, its facts and preview go to stderr so the user sees what they confirm.
32	- Ticking no packages in add re-asks instead of E273.
33	Accepted limits (documented, not built): resize mid-prompt redraws on the next key; the editor temp file can leak if the terminal is closed while the editor is open.
34	
35	Rendering (decided 2026-11-24)
36	- Callisto does no terminal sizing and never rewrites labels: full package names are shown and filtered; inquire's default page size; inquire wraps long labels.
37	- Documented limits of the prompt library: resizing mid-prompt or a pane under about 10 rows can misdraw; use a bigger pane or pass --package/--summary.

2	
3	1. Secrets: no user-supplied URL, remote, token, env value or path that may carry credentials is printed in any message, error, JSON or log. Print only values we derived ourselves (owner/repo slug, package names). Child processes get the runner's filtered environment.
4	2. Same structure for preview and real: dry runs, hints and previews compute on exactly the set/plan the real command uses (selection, group expansion, publishable packages, roster). No second derivation.
5	3. Modes: text vs --format json vs non-TTY. JSON stdout stays a single document; human notes go to stderr once in both modes; json never prompts. Check every new message in all three modes.
6	4. Validation order: mode/eligibility first, then input validation, then prompts or side effects. A bad input never reaches a confirmation screen.
7	5. Optional conveniences (preselection, detection, previews, hints) degrade with a warning; they never make the command fail.
8	6. Never parse text we rendered, and never hand-parse a foreign grammar (Markdown, git URLs, shell) beyond the coarse classification we need; prefer the owning tool or omit.
9	7. Rust: exhaustive match on our own enums (no _ arm); no unwrap outside tests; expect names its invariant; no swallowed errors (.ok(), drop(result)) without a one-line reason; no process::exit outside main; Drop-based cleanup; no global mutable state unless unavoidable; minimal visibility.
10	8. Edge inputs for anything touching user paths or strings: spaces, newlines, leading ':' or '-', unicode, empty, very long.
11	9. Tests: one test per behaviour through the real binary where users see it; tests clean up children and temp files on failure.
12	11. # Interactive CLI contract (add, init) - decided 2026-11-23, owner-approved direction

When prompts run
- stdin AND stderr are terminals and output is text: prompts.
- --format json, or stdin or stderr not a terminal: never prompt. add without flags -> E214; init without --yes -> E240; each names the flags to pass.
- Blank or whitespace --summary: error before any prompt.

Ending a run
- Completed: path written; next-step line on stderr; exit 0.
- Esc or Ctrl-C at any prompt: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 130.
- Declining the review / write confirmation: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
- Editor saves nothing or exits non-zero: "Cancelled, nothing written."; exit 0.
- External kill -INT at a prompt: default signal behaviour (signal 2), nothing written; documented limit: terminal may need `reset`.
- SIGINT while $EDITOR runs (unix): ignored by Callisto (git launch_editor precedent); the editor decides. No signal thread anywhere.

Editor and inputs
- $VISUAL else $EDITOR; blank = unset; none -> inline summary prompt.
- Unusable editor (split error, not found, non-UTF-8): one warning naming the variable and command, then the inline prompt, answers kept.
- Whitespace-only inline summary: re-prompt.
- Changed packages first and marked (Enter keeps them), exactly as status reports; detection failure -> one warning, none marked.
- JSON mode: exactly one report on stdout; notes once on stderr.

init and origin
- Missing or non-hosted origin: one note; preview and init continue unbound; the remote value is never printed.
- --workflow / --artifact-target without a hosted origin: E299, help names git remote get-url --push origin / set-url --push.

Exit codes: 0 success or decline; 1 error; 2 usage; 130 cancelled at a prompt.

Proposed additions (2026-11-24, pending owner approval)
- TERM=dumb never prompts (E214/E240), as non-TTY.
- While init prompts, its facts and preview go to stderr so the user sees what they confirm.
- Ticking no packages in add re-asks instead of E273.
Accepted limits (documented, not built): resize mid-prompt redraws on the next key; the editor temp file can leak if the terminal is closed while the editor is open.

Rendering (decided 2026-11-24, revised 2026-11-24)
- Unbounded lists (add's packages, majors, minors; init's product package) are line-based, as `git add -i`: printed once to stderr, numbered, full names, marked items starred; one typed line of numbers, ranges (1-3) or names separated by spaces or commas; Enter keeps the marked; an invalid answer re-asks with a short reason; an escape-sequence key (arrow) re-asks.

- No cursor movement, redraw or sizing code for lists, so terminal size and resizing have no limits there.
